Dalang is partially supported by the Swiss National Foundation for Scientific Research, the research of C. Mueller is partially supported by a Simons grant, and Y. Xiao is partially supported by NSF grants DMS-1607089 and DMS-185
arxiv-1911-09793.creator: Robert C. Dalang, Cheuk Yin Lee, Carl Mueller, and Yimin Xiao
arxiv-1911-09793.description: Abstract . This paper is concerned with the existence of multiple points of Gaussian random fields. Under the framework of Dalang et al. (2017), we prove that, for a wide class of Gaussian random fields, multiple points do not exist in critical dimensions.

arxiv-2009-07473.title: Solomon at SemEval-2020 Task 11: Ensemble Architecture for Fine-Tuned Propaganda Detection in News Articles
arxiv-2009-07473.creator: Mayank Raj Ankita Gupta Ajay Jaiswal Sudeep Kumar Sahoo Rohit R.R Vertika Srivastava Yeon Hyang KimSamsung R&D Institute India, Bangalore { mayank.raj, ajay.jaiswal, rohit.r.r,gupta.ankita, sudeep.sahoo, v.srivastava, purine.kim}@samsung.com
arxiv-2009-07473.description: Abstract This paper describes our system (Solomon) details and results of participation in the SemEval 2020 Task 11 ”Detection of Propaganda Techniques in News Articles” [ \citenameDa San Martino et al.2020 ] . We participated in Task ”Technique Classification” (TC) which is a multi-class classification task.

arxiv-2107-02468.title: Existence, stability and regularity of periodic solutions for nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations
arxiv-2107-02468.creator: Eric Luçon, Christophe Poquet
arxiv-2107-02468.description: Abstract . We consider a class of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations describing the dynamics of an infinite population of units within mean-field interaction. Relying on a slow-fast viewpoint and on the theory of approximately invariant manifolds we obtain the existence of a stable periodic solution for the PDE, consisting of probability measures.

arxiv-2204-01076.title: On Angles in Higher Order Brillouin Tessellations and Related Tilings in the Plane Work by all authors but the second is supported by the European Research Council (ERC), grant no. 788183, by the Wittgenstein Prize, Austrian Science Fund (FWF), grant no. Z 342-N31, and by the DFG Collaborative Resea
arxiv-2204-01076.creator: Herbert Edelsbrunner, Alexey Garber, Mohadese Ghafari, Teresa Heiss, Morteza Saghafian
arxiv-2204-01076.description: Abstract For a locally finite set in ℝ 2 {{\mathbb{R}}}^{2} , the order- k k Brillouin tessellations form an infinite sequence of convex face-to-face tilings of the plane. If the set is coarsely dense and generic, then the corresponding infinite sequences of minimum and maximum angles are both monotonic in k k .

arxiv-2307-16720.title: Clustering multivariate functional data with the epigraph and hypograph indices: a case study on Madrid air quality.
arxiv-2307-16720.creator: Belén Pulido, Alba M. Franco-Pereira, Rosa E. Lillo
arxiv-2307-16720.description: Abstract With the rapid growth of data generation, advancements in functional data analysis (FDA) have become essential, especially for approaches that handle multiple variables at the same time. This paper introduces a novel formulation of the epigraph and hypograph indices, along with their generalized expressions, specifically designed for multivariate functional data (MFD).

arxiv-2410-00562.title: Forbidden Minor Characterization of 3-fold-3-splitting of Binary Gammoid
arxiv-2410-00562.description: Abstract . The r-fold-n-point-splitting operation is an important operation in Graph Theory defined by Slater [ 15 ] . Later, Ghafari [ 6 ] extended 3-fold-n-point-splitting operation in binary matroids and obtained the result for Eulerian matroids whose 3-fold is Eulerian.

arxiv-2505-00118.title: A new look at the SU 2 gauge monopole
arxiv-2505-00118.creator: W. F. Kao
arxiv-2505-00118.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by W. F. Kao. An S ​ U 2 × U 1 SU_{2}\times U_{1} scalar vector model with a scalar doublet φ \varphi is reviewed for the study of possible magnetic monopole solution. An eigenvalue equation n ^ a ​ σ a ​ φ ± = ± φ ± \hat{n}^{a}\sigma^{a}\varphi_{\pm}=\pm\varphi_{\pm} is shown to induce a set of monopole solutions specified by the unit vector n ^ \hat{n} .

arxiv-2509-20884.title: Integrating Object Interaction Self-Attention and GAN-Based Debiasing for Visual Question Answering
arxiv-2509-20884.creator: Zhifei Li, Feng Qiu, Yiran Wang, Yujing Xia, Kui Xiao, Miao Zhang, Yan Zhang
arxiv-2509-20884.description: Abstract Visual Question Answering (VQA) presents a unique challenge by requiring models to understand and reason about visual content to answer questions accurately. Existing VQA models often struggle with biases introduced by the training data, leading to over-reliance on superficial patterns and inadequate generalization to diverse questions and images.

arxiv-2510-20499.title: GPU-Accelerated Primal Heuristics for Mixed Integer Programming
arxiv-2510-20499.creator: Akif Çördük, Piotr Sielski, Alice Boucher, Kumar Aatish
arxiv-2510-20499.description: Abstract We introduce a fusion of GPU accelerated primal heuristics for Mixed Integer Programming. Leveraging GPU acceleration enables exploration of larger search regions and faster iterations. A GPU-accelerated PDLP serves as an approximate LP solver, while a new probing cache facilitates rapid roundings and early infeasibility detection.

arxiv-2604-17219.creator: Chenyang Wang, Yun Yang

pmc-10614676.title: Universal theranostic CRISPR/Cas13a RNA-editing system for glioma
pmc-10614676.creator: Ye Wu, Yunfei Wang, Junhu Zhou, Jianhao Wang, Qi Zhan, Qixue Wang, Eryan Yang, Weili Jin, Fei Tong, Jixing Zhao, Biao Hong, Junrui Liu, Chunsheng Kang
pmc-10614676.description: Background: The CRISPR/Cas13a system offers the advantages of rapidity, precision, high sensitivity, and programmability as a molecular diagnostic tool for critical illnesses. One of the salient features of CRISPR/Cas13a-based bioassays is its ability to recognize and cleave the target RNA specifically.

pmc-11388194.title: Deciphering the relative importance of genetic elements in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae to guide countermeasure development
pmc-11388194.creator: Thomas A. Russo, Ulrike Carlino-MacDonald, Zachary J. Drayer, Connor J. Davies, Cassandra L. Alvarado, Alan Hutson, Ting L. Luo, Melissa J. Martin, Patrick T. McGann, Francois Lebreton
pmc-11388194.description: SummaryBackgroundQuantitating the contribution of phenotype-responsible elements in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae is needed.MethodsIsogenic mutants of four hypervirulent clinical isolates that produced K1 (ST23), K2 (ST86), K20 (ST1544), or K54 (ST29) capsules (mean 2.2 log10 LD50 (range 1.5–2.9)) were created to measure the effects on LD50 in a murine model of the hypervirulence-associated plasmid (pVir), iucA, prmpA, prmpA2 (truncated), irp2, and clbBC.

pmc-11444487.title: Regional morphological adaptations of vastus lateralis muscle in response to different progressive resistance training programs: A randomised controlled trial
pmc-11444487.creator: R Longrak, W Sonchan, W Jaidee
pmc-11444487.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundResistance training often increases muscle size, a phenomenon known as muscle hypertrophy. These morphological adaptations were typically documented to occur in a non-uniform pattern. pmc-12362988.title: The role of visual experience in haptic spatial perception: evidence from early blind, late blind, and sighted individuals
pmc-12362988.creator: Lara A. Coelho, Daniela E. Aguilar Ramirez, Serena Basta, Marta Guarischi, Claudia L. R. Gonzalez, Monica Gori
pmc-12362988.description: There is contradictory evidence on the effect that visual experience has on haptic abilities. Indeed, some studies have documented that a lack of vision (blindness) results in decreased haptic perception, whereas other studies report an enhanced haptic ability in blind individuals. To examine the role of vision in haptic spatial processing, we recruited early blind, late blind, and sighted participants.

pmc-12558150.title: Understanding and redressing imbalances for South–North collaborations in energy and development research
pmc-12558150.creator: Muez Ali, Tash Perros, Penlope Yaguma, Tiago B. Diniz, Lilia C. Couto, Harshavardhan Jatkar, Jennifer Cronin, Pamela Fennell, Alexandre Szklo, Yacob Mulugetta
pmc-12558150.description: The Global South–Global North divide is widely defined using the Brandt Line, which proposed a geographical divide between more developed countries in the North and less developed countries in the South. Inequities in South–North research collaborations manifest in different ways and at different stages.

pmc-12610753.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Talc Slurry Pleurodesis in the Treatment of Patients with Malignant Pleural Effusion and Low Karnofsky Performance Status Scores
pmc-12610753.creator: Eliza Kastrati, Antigona Hasani, Fadil Gradica, Tefta Isufaj Haliti, Aidana Bolat, Ilir Hoxha, Takeshi Saraya
pmc-12610753.description: Background/Objectives: Malignant pleural effusion is a common and distressing complication of advanced cancer, often resulting in severe symptoms such as dyspnoea, which significantly impacts patients’ quality of life. This study evaluates the effectiveness and safety of talc slurry pleurodesis as a palliative treatment for recurrent malignant pleural effusion and examines predictive factors for pleurodesis success and survival.

pmc-12747808.title: Prognostic Factors and Optimal Empiric Therapy for Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL)-Producing Enterobacterales Bacteremia
pmc-12747808.creator: Tadashi Maeda, Sohei Harada, Dai Nakase, Yusuke Nakamura, Takeo Mori, Katsuhito Kashiwagi, Takahiro Sato, Taito Miyazaki, Yosuke Sasaki
pmc-12747808.description: BackgroundBloodstream infections (BSIs) caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producingEnterobacterales (ESBL-E) are associated with increased morbidity and mortality, yet the optimal empiric treatment strategy remains uncertain. We aimed to identify prognostic factors for early clinical response and 30-day mortality in patients with ESBL-E bacteremia and to evaluate the impact of the appropriateness of empiric antimicrobial therapy.

pmc-12772178.title: Dimerization-activated PP2C-D2 and D5 phosphatases negatively regulate brassinosteroid signaling by antagonizing BRI1
pmc-12772178.creator: Mengzhan Li, Chunli Liu, Shelley R. Hepworth, Yuting Yang, Li Wei, Jim P. Fouracre, Suo-Min Wang, Jia Li, Hongju Yin
pmc-12772178.description: SignificanceReversible protein phosphorylation mediated by kinases and phosphatases is essential for plant growth and development. While plant phospho-signaling research has largely focused on kinases and phosphorylation, phosphatases and dephosphorylation are comparatively understudied. Here, we show that protein phosphatase PP2C-Ds are activated by dimerization.

pmc-13081536.title: The spatiotemporal dynamics of MAMs: mechanisms, pathologies, and therapeutic rewiring
pmc-13081536.creator: Dongxue Xu, Yinye Huang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Benzheng Liu, Mingying Wang, Yiming Li, Zhiyong Peng
pmc-13081536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes (MAMs) constitute highly dynamic signaling hubs that coordinate a spatiotemporal network regulating calcium flux, lipid trafficking, and innate immune activation. Beyond functioning as physical organelle tethers, the plasticity of MAMs is essential for cellular resilience. Notably, maladaptive remodeling of these contacts, which presents a spatiotemporal paradox in that both pathological tightening and excessive dissociation can precipitate dysfunction, underlies the pathogenesis of diverse complex diseases, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular failure, and kidney injury.

pmc-13332148.title: Research on longitudinal bowing defect of aluminum alloy plate in roll-forming asymmetric corrugated channels
pmc-13332148.creator: Chi Ma, Chuntian Xu, Xu Zong, Mengfei Huang, Dapeng Zheng
pmc-13332148.description: Longitudinal bowing defect (LBD) is commonly produced during the continuous roll forming of materials, which directly affects the quality of the formed products. The asymmetric corrugated channels (ACCs) have a large number of channels and are subjected to the pressure of asymmetric rollers. Therefore, the control of LBD is more complex compared to single channel during the roll forming.

pmc-13365401.title: Soluble TREM2 engages cell-surface nucleolin to drive vascular permeability and malignant ascites in ovarian cancer
pmc-13365401.creator: Qianqian Li, Yubo Zhang, Hui Luo, Yongjian Wu, Jingbo Qin, Lijie Wang, Qianqian Zhang, Ting Yu, Xi Huang, Shuang Guo, Bingfan Xie, Huanhuan He
pmc-13365401.description: Ascites, a hallmark of advanced ovarian cancer, severely impairs patient quality of life and contributes to therapeutic resistance. Current management strategies remain primarily palliative, highlighting the urgent need to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Although TREM2+ macrophages are enriched in malignant ascites, the role of soluble TREM2 (sTREM2) in regulating vascular function and ascites pathogenesis remains poorly understood.

pmc-13473212.title: Aging-Related Choroidal Heterogeneity and Loss: An Investigative Global Human Choroidal Thickness Review (ARCHLIGHT Study)
pmc-13473212.creator: Abbie Lai, Mariam Issa, Ahmad Ali, Austin Pereira, Alaa Al Ali, Jay Chhablani, Peng Yan
pmc-13473212.description: Purpose:To synthesize current evidence on the pathophysiology, clinical relevance, and implications for age-related choroidal thinning.Methods:A systematic literature search of relevant publications was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library, up to and including May 2024. Identified studies reported choroidal thickness changes with aging.

pmc-13515927.title: A 67–110 GHz Multi-Carrier Communication Front End Based on Broadband Diplexer and Filtering Waveguide-to-Microstrip Transitions
pmc-13515927.creator: Yujie Zhi, Yulong Zhong, Bo Zhang, Yibo Fan, Zuqiang Ou, Jincai Qiao
pmc-13515927.description: This paper presents a 67–110 GHz millimeter-wave RF front end for 6G high-speed wireless communications. A broadband diplexer based on a staggered branch-waveguide structure is first proposed to achieve low insertion loss and high isolation simultaneously. The fabricated diplexer exhibits better than 12 dB return loss, 48.6% fractional bandwidth, and less than 1.5 dB insertion loss.
